title: AGA clinical practice update on de-prescribing of proton pump inhibitors: expert review
authors: Targownik LE, Fisher DA, Saini SD
funder: Not read: the publisher page refused access and the article is not in PubMed Central; PubMed lists VA HSR&D grant I01 HX002693.
result: Not a systematic review; no formal rating of evidence quality. Best practice advice: every PPI user should have regular review and documentation of the indication by the primary care provider; patients without a definitive indication should be considered for a trial of de-prescribing; most twice-daily users with an indication should step down to once daily; complicated GERD, Barrett's oesophagus, eosinophilic oesophagitis or idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and high upper gastrointestinal bleeding risk generally exclude de-prescribing; patients should be told they may develop transient symptoms from rebound acid hypersecretion; tapering or abrupt discontinuation can be considered. Advice 10: the decision to discontinue should be based solely on lack of an indication and not on concern for PPI-associated adverse events; a past or present adverse event or its risk factors is not an independent indication for withdrawal.
